context:
Goal: each role runs the least model that keeps it accurate.
Problem (money): your layout puts the coordinator on Sonnet high, but the coordinator writes every lane brief and reads your rulings by meaning, and nothing checks a brief against the rulings until lane brief-from-step's judge lands. Its 12:07 "close after merge" brief was stricter than your Nov 9 words.
Your layout (13:41 CST, via the retrospective): coordinator Sonnet high, arbiter Opus medium, consultant Opus medium, triage Sonnet high, guard and check lanes Sonnet high, product and design lanes Sonnet medium. Your question: any you would strongly argue need Opus that do not?
Triage's answer: only the coordinator, and only until the brief judge exists. The blind role ranking put it first. Everything else in your layout reads fine to me; triage on Sonnet high matches how this session has run. Unmeasured.
Also unmapped: the batch runner and docs lanes. The retrospective suggests Sonnet medium for both.
Based on (measured): the coordinator's 12:07 slip is that lane's red case. Based on (read): the blind ranking put the coordinator first.
Departs from: main, where the coordinator, triage and consultant take the main model (Opus) by the "separate sessions" row, the arbiter runs Opus high, and all lanes run Sonnet medium — your rows, plus guard lanes at high.
Meanwhile: nothing changes until you pick; the rows land in decision agent-model-cap (home: step role-gaps-from-ranking). Past rulings not read by triage.

options.gain: Briefs stay right while no check exists.
options.label: Your layout, but the coordinator runs Opus high until the brief judge goes red on a bad brief, then Sonnet high (recommended)
options.lose: Opus cost on one session for that time.

options.label: Your layout as written
options.lose: A brief that drops your words goes unchecked until the judge lands.

options.gain: Rare clash rulings get full depth.
options.label: Your layout, plus the arbiter at high

reply: Closed 13:5x CST as a duplicate of item 747, where you answered (your 13:53 CST words, relayed by the retrospective): the layout is ruling own-747-role-layout, so the coordinator runs Sonnet high. It sets session rows only; agents keep their agent-model-cap rows (Explore, test-author, reviewer and record-writer Haiku xhigh; builder Sonnet high; Plan, designer, design-reviewer and refuter Opus high). The scope line goes in the record when the rows land.
short: Which model each role runs: your layout, with the coordinator on Opus for now?
title: Which model should each role run, and should the coordinator stay on Opus until the brief check exists?
why: Sets the model rows in decision agent-model-cap; the coordinator's choice changes cost and brief accuracy.
